Coordinates release of remains with appropriate services/outside agencies in the event of autopsy, or organ/tissue/body donation.

Council for Veterans that have been adjudicated as incompetent. This may require the position to appear in-person at county court houses.

Für Menschen, die Service nicht verwalten, sondern prägen.
Support wird oft unterschätzt.
Dabei entscheidet genau dieser Moment darüber, wie sich eine Zusammenarbeit anfühlt. Wenn etwas nicht funktioniert. Wenn eine Frage auftaucht. Wenn ein Hotel einfach jemanden braucht, der zuhört, versteht und eine Lösung findet.
Genau dort beginnt unsere Arbeit.
Wir sind HotelNetSolutions aus Berlin. Seit 2006 entwickeln wir Software für die Hotellerie. Keine Software von der Stange, sondern Lösungen, die sich den Hotels anpassen und nicht umgekehrt. Mit OnePageBooking, VoucherBooking, RateDistributor und der MultiPropertyView unterstützen wir heute mehr als 2.200 Hotels und Hotelgruppen dabei, mehr Direktbuchungen zu erzielen und ihre Persönlichkeit auch im Internet erlebbar zu machen.
Wir glauben nicht an anonyme Tickets. Wir glauben an Beziehungen. An Erreichbarkeit. An das gesprochene Wort. Und daran, dass guter Support weit mehr ist als die Antwort auf eine Frage.
Deshalb suchen wir keinen Verwalter.
Wir suchen einen Head of Customer Support, der Menschen entwickelt, Prozesse hinterfragt und gemeinsam mit seinem Team dafür sorgt, dass aus jedem Kontakt ein gutes Gefühl entsteht.
Aufgaben
Du führst unser internationales Customer Support Team mit Klarheit, Vertrauen und einem offenen Ohr. Du schaffst ein Umfeld, in dem Menschen gerne Verantwortung übernehmen und ihr Wissen miteinander teilen.
Du erkennst, wo Prozesse haken, bevor sie zum Problem werden. Gemeinsam mit deinem Team entwickelst du unseren Support kontinuierlich weiter und sorgst dafür, dass Qualität kein Zufall ist.
Du behältst Kennzahlen im Blick, ohne dabei den Menschen dahinter zu vergessen. Denn jede Zahl erzählt eine Geschichte. Man muss nur genau hinsehen.
Du arbeitest eng mit Produktmanagement, Entwicklung und Vertrieb zusammen. Kundenfeedback landet bei dir nicht in einer Schublade, sondern dort, wo Produkte besser werden.
Auch wenn es einmal kompliziert wird, bleibst du ruhig. Du begleitest Eskalationen mit Souveränität und findest Lösungen, die langfristig tragen.
Qualifikation
Du hast bereits ein Customer Support oder Customer Success Team geführt und weißt, dass gute Führung nicht bedeutet, auf jede Frage selbst die Antwort zu kennen.
Du hast Freude daran, Menschen wachsen zu sehen und ihnen den Rücken freizuhalten.
Idealerweise kennst du die Hotellerie oder ein Softwareunternehmen, das erklärungsbedürftige Produkte betreut. Du verstehst, wie wichtig verlässlicher Support für den Alltag unserer Kunden ist.
Du arbeitest strukturiert, denkst analytisch und triffst Entscheidungen mit Ruhe und Augenmaß.
Du kommunizierst klar, wertschätzend und verbindlich. Auf Deutsch mindestens auf C1 Niveau. Englisch hilft dir im internationalen Austausch.
Vor allem aber hast du Lust, Dinge besser zu machen. Nicht weil es im Prozesshandbuch steht, sondern weil du weißt, dass guter Service den Unterschied macht.

Ein guter Support entsteht nicht durch Prozesse allein.
Er entsteht durch Menschen, die sich gegenseitig vertrauen. Die gerne zusammenarbeiten. Die auch an stressigen Tagen miteinander lachen. Genau so arbeiten wir.
Dich erwartet ein Team, das sich gegenseitig unterstützt, Wissen teilt und gemeinsam Lösungen findet. Ehrlich gesagt finden wir sogar, dass es das beste Team aller Zeiten ist. Wahrscheinlich sagen das viele. Wir meinen es wirklich.
Wir suchen Menschen, die bleiben möchten. Deshalb erhältst du einen unbefristeten Arbeitsvertrag und eine langfristige Perspektive in einem inhabergeführten Unternehmen, in dem Zuverlässigkeit nicht nur auf der Website steht, sondern gelebt wird.
Treue soll sich lohnen. Deshalb wächst mit der Zeit auch dein Urlaubsanspruch.
Nach Feierabend ist Feierabend. Unsere Arbeitszeiten sind montags bis freitags geregelt. Überstunden kannst du in Freizeit umwandeln. Das Wochenende gehört dir.
Zwei Tage Home Office. Drei Tage gemeinsam im Büro. Für uns die richtige Mischung aus konzentriertem Arbeiten und persönlichem Austausch.
Unser Berliner Loft im Tiergarten hat den Charme eines echten Hinterhofs. Keine Hochglanzbüros. Dafür kurze Wege, offene Türen und Menschen, die man gerne trifft.
Dresscode? Komm so, wie du dich wohlfühlst. Hoodie funktioniert bei uns genauso gut wie Hemd.
Mitreden gehört bei uns dazu. Bei großen Entscheidungen genauso wie bei der Frage, welche Süßigkeiten als Nächstes im Büro landen.
Und weil Zusammenarbeit mehr ist als Meetings, verbringen wir auch außerhalb des Arbeitsalltags gerne Zeit miteinander. Mal auf der Spree. Mal beim Bowling. Und manchmal einfach bei unserer inzwischen legendären Kuchenparty.

Every year, we sponsor 2 remote UX apprentices from anywhere in the world to join us for 7 months, either in the fall or spring seasons or online. Our UX apprentices work through the end-to-end UX design and UX research process for a startup idea of their choice that will help them attract hiring managers in that topic space or industry.
Apprentices take our program for free and receive 1:1 mentorship throughout the 7-month program. Alumni UX apprentices go on to make between $85,000 -$130,000 in UX design, product design, UX research, or service design roles after they complete the program.
We are committed to helping women, immigrants, POC, and LGBTQ folks break into tech and land 6-figure UX jobs. We help you land 6-figure UX jobs or coach you till you get it.

This apprenticeship program is open to new grads and UX career changers alike! Here are some apprenticeship requirements to keep in mind before applying:

Interested in creative career paths in UX research, UX design, product design or service design
Willing to commit 5-10 hours of work per week to complete program deliverables
Willing to attend 2-3 hour weekend lectures to learn the end-to-end design process OR willing to complete online video course modules
Open to feedback from UX mentors and demonstrates a willingness to revise design work

Build digital products and services 0-1
Lead end-to-end design process for a startup idea or topic of your choice
Lead product scoping and feature scoping, as well as entire project management
Identify target market for product and position product for launch success
Incorporate AI tools into your UX design process
Design AI features and products by considering AI specific design parameters and heuristics
Understand how AI works and advocate for ethical AI design that builds trust without over-reliance with users
Develop a business model for the product or service and demonstrate how the product/service will scale as the business model scales
Lead discovery research by managing user recruitment, creating research plans, writing interview guides, leading 8-16 discovery interviews, and synthesizing interview insights
Deliver a compelling UX design and business pitch for your startup idea, showcasing both qualitative and quantitative data to justify the problem space and the solution
Tell a compelling story about users by showcasing user types, personas, stakeholder maps, journey maps, process maps, service blueprints, ideation matrixes, sketches, wireframes, UX workflows, prototypes and other visual deliverables
Lead user testing of wireframes and prototypes to improve product/service usability and constantly iterate on your startup idea
Design a unique design system for your solution from scratch, creating components, a style guide, and branding for your solution
Analyze direct and indirect competitors to clearly articulate your solution’s differentiators and why your solution is innovative and more likely to succeed over competing options

Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected.

See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities Current U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) employees with competitive status.

Current Civilian Employees of the Command Domestic Defense Industrial Base/Major Range and Test Facilities Base Civilian Personnel Workforce Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act Military Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473 Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Reserve (MR) and National Guard (NG) Technician Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD MR and NG Preference Eligible Tech Receiving Disability Retirement Priority Placement Program, DoD Retained Grade Preference Eligible Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) of 1998 In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document.

General Experience for GS-05: Three years progressively responsible experience, 1 year of which was equivalent to at least the GS-04 grade level, which includes at least two of the following:1) Assisting with employee or position personnel actions and maintaining tracking systems for required action; OR 2) Compiling administrative or budget information for higher level review; OR 3) Providing administrative support to managers and employees on workforce-related matters.

This definition of general experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-04). OR Education: Four-year course of study leading to a bachelor's degree.

OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 36.

Then divide your total number of completed undergraduate semester hours (or equivalent) by 120. Add the two percentages.

Specialized Experience for GS-07: One year of specialized experience which includes at least two of the following: 1) Reviewing and processing employee or position actions using automated personnel or financial systems; OR 2) Compiling and analyzing reports related to staffing, manpower, budgets, or organizational operations; OR 3) Advising supervisors or employees on routine administrative or workforce management procedures.

This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-05).

OR Education: One full academic year of graduate-level education in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as, Business Administration, Human Resource Management, or a closely related field.

(Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) OR Superior Academic Achievement: Successful completion of all the requirements for a bachelor's degree with Superior Academic Achievement.

In order to be creditable under this provision, Superior Academic Achievement must have been gained in a curriculum that is qualifying for the position to be filled, such as that identified in Education above.

Superior Academic Achievement is based on: (1) Class Standing - Applicants must be in the upper third of the graduating class in the college, university, or major subdivision, such as the College of Liberal Arts or the School of Business Administration, based on completed courses; OR (2) Grade-Point Average (G.P.A.) - Applicants must have a grade-point average of either (a) 3.0 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B" or better) as recorded on your official transcript, or as computed based on 4 years of education, or as computed based on courses completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum; or (b) 3.5 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B+" or better) based on the average of the required courses completed in the major field or the required courses in the major field completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum; OR (3) Honor Society Membership - Applicants may be considered eligible based on membership in one of the approved national scholastic honor societies listed by the Association of College Honor Societies (https://www.achsnatl.org/).

OR Combination of Education and Experience: Specialized experience as described above, but less than one year; and I have some graduate education as described above, but less than the required one year.

I have computed the percentage of the requirements that I meet, and the total is at least 100% (To compute the percentage, divide your total months of qualifying experience by 12. Then, divide your semester hours of graduate education by 18. Add the two percentages. The total percentage must equal at least 100 percent to qualify.).

(Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) Specialized Experience for GS-09: One year of specialized experience which includes at least two of the following: 1) Analyzing workforce, budget, or organizational data to recommend solutions or management actions; OR 2) Utilizing automated systems to process personnel, manpower, or financial transactions; OR 3) Collaborating with management, human resources, or other offices to resolve workforce management matters and support organizational changes.

This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-07).

OR Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Business Management or Human Resource Management.

OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12.

Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages. Time in Grade Requirement: Time-In-Grade requirement must be met by the closing date of this announcement.

Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) Position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade GS-04 for GS-05, GS-05 for GS-07, or GS-07 for GS-09 (or equivalent).

With regards to time-in-grade validation, if you held a position other than a GS pay plan, be sure your resume includes the pay plan and the salary you earned during the assignment. Without this information, your time-in-grade validation may not be able to be verified and will result in your not meeting the time-grade requirement for this vacancy.

A further explanation of the required time in grade documentation can be found under the Required Documents section of this announcement.

This is your chance to be the backbone of the operation—bringing order, accuracy, and a personal touch to a team that truly values great service. If you thrive in fast-paced environments and love being the calm in the storm, this is where you belong. 🚀

The FEMA Call Center Customer Service Representative (CSR) serves as a direct telephone point of contact for individuals registering for federal disaster assistance, callers seeking information about a prior registration, and individuals seeking referrals to disaster relief programs and other assistance providers.

The CSR conducts customer interactions with patience, tact, courtesy, and professionalism; determines the caller's needs; provides approved instructions and referrals; and accurately enters information into FEMA-approved computer systems while following a scripted interview process.
The CSR performs work in direct support of FEMA's Individual Assistance mission during periods of disaster activity. Depending on the applicable Call Order, assigned duties may include Registration Intake (RI), Basic Helpline (HL), Transitional Sheltering Assistance (TSA), outbound calling, document review or validation, case-related support, and referrals to other disaster assistance providers.

Serve as a direct point of contact for disaster survivors and other callers seeking federal assistance, registration services, status information, or referrals.
Conduct every call with patience, tact, courtesy, empathy, and professionalism.
Listen actively and determine the caller's needs using approved procedures and scripts.
Provide accurate instructions, information, telephone numbers, and referrals based on current FEMA-approved guidance.
Conduct scripted interviews and collect required information from callers.
Accurately enter caller-provided information into FEMA's Windows-compatible database or other FEMA-approved systems.
Complete required data entry and other call-agent work while the caller is on the telephone, except for limited after-call work permitted by the contract.

s.h: Perform Registration Intake (RI) duties when assigned.
s.t:
Perform Basic Helpline (HL) duties when assigned, including assisting callers with questions concerning prior registrations.
Perform Transitional Sheltering Assistance (TSA) or other specialized lines of business when authorized and trained.
Conduct outbound calls when assigned.
Perform document review, document validation, or other specialized processing functions when assigned and trained.
Provide referrals to appropriate secondary support organizations and other disaster assistance providers.
Attend required pre-shift meetings and briefings and remain current on event-specific information, priorities, procedures, and policy changes.
Follow FEMA-approved scripts, job aids, Standard Operating Procedures, work instructions, and supervisor direction.
Maintain required availability and readiness to receive calls during assigned production periods.
Meet applicable customer service, quality, productivity, attendance, schedule-adherence, and call-handling standards.
Participate in quality monitoring, coaching, calibration, remedial training, and performance-improvement activities.
Immediately report system, security, privacy, technical, or operational issues through established CRI procedures.
Perform other related duties assigned in response to FEMA's level of support and the requirements of the applicable Call Order.

Protect FEMA Personally Identifiable Information (PII), Sensitive but Unclassified (SBU) information, and other protected information always.
Access FEMA information only when authorized and when access is necessary to perform assigned duties.
Do not retain PII or other information from calls outside authorized FEMA systems and procedures.
Do not create or retain handwritten or electronic notes containing caller PII unless expressly authorized by the contract and applicable procedures.
Immediately destroy any permitted temporary notes in accordance with FEMA requirements.
Do not discuss or expose FEMA caller information to unauthorized persons.
Perform all work in an approved environment that satisfies FEMA/HSPD-12 security requirements.
Never handle FEMA calls from a public environment or another location where unauthorized persons may hear or access protected information.
Comply with all DHS, FEMA, CRI, HSPD-12, cybersecurity, privacy, and information-security requirements.
Immediately report suspected security incidents, unauthorized disclosure, lost equipment, improper access, or other security concerns.

Must be a United States Citizen.
Lawful permanent resident are not eligible for this FEMA assignment.
Must be at least 18 years of age.
Must successfully complete the FEMA-required background investigation and receive the required favorable adjudication before receiving access to protected FEMA information or systems.
Not in default on federal student loans.

No felony convictions within the past 7 years.
Misdemeanor convictions within the past 7 years may impact eligibility.
No non-medical collections totaling $7,500 or more.

Must comply with any additional security, suitability, background-investigation, or access requirements established by a specific FEMA Call Order.

Twenty years ago, the first selections of Les Composantes were born. A story born from a thirst for independence and a passion for vintage. An instinctive way of circulating clothes, guided by a particular attention to what lasts.

As a Front Line Manager you will: Plan work to be accomplished by subordinates, sets and adjusts short-term priorities and prepares schedules for completion of work. Evaluate work performance of subordinates and makes recommendations for outstanding performance recognition and/or disciplinary action. Give advice, counsel or instruction to employees on work and administrative matters.

Interview candidates for positions within the organization/unit and recommend appointment, promotion or reassignment to such positions. Hear and resolve complaints from employees, refer group grievances and/or more serious unresolved complaints as appropriate.

Effect minor disciplinary measures, such as warnings and reprimands, recommend other actions in more serious cases. Identify developmental and training needs of employees, providing or arranging for needed development and training. Initiate ways to improve production, work processes and/or to increase the quality of the work directed.

The following are the job specific duties of this position. You will have the opportunity to learn to perform these duties and receive training to help you grow in this position. Provides leadership and direction to employees performing technical work involving taxpayer inquiries, case analysis, and resolution of complex tax issues.

Plans, organizes, and assigns work based on program priorities, workload complexity, and employee capabilities to ensure timely and accurate completion of assignments.

Monitors work in progress and reviews completed work for quality, accuracy, and adherence to applicable tax laws, regulations, and Internal Revenue Manual (IRM) procedures, taking corrective action as needed.

Ensures timely and accurate resolution of inventory and monitors aged inventory using available reports and systems to prevent overage conditions. Provides technical oversight of taxpayer inquiries and case resolution activities by evaluating work performed and ensuring consistent application of tax laws, regulations, and IRM procedures.

Reviews and analyzes cases involving multiple issue areas, complex regulatory requirements, and frequently changing guidance to ensure accurate and compliant resolution. Ensures employees follow established procedures for handling inventory, system usage, and case documentation requirements.

Analyzes workload, production data, and program trends to assess performance, identify risks, and recommend improvements. Uses automated systems and reports to monitor inventory, evaluate productivity, and support data-driven decisions.

Obtains and analyzes quality review data (e.g., Embedded Quality, National Quality, and other review systems) to identify errors, trends, and opportunities for improvement, and provides feedback to employees. Manages administrative functions, including leave, time and attendance, and staffing, and resolves employee concerns at the appropriate level.

Performs conduct and leave counseling, and promotes a work environment that supports employee engagement, motivation, and retention. Applies advanced interviewing and analytical techniques to evaluate taxpayer circumstances, including sensitive financial and personal information, and to determine appropriate actions.

Ensures proper handling of cases involving issues such as compliance determinations, financial hardship, or potential noncompliance. Evaluates determinations made by employees to ensure sound judgment in resolving discrepancies and interpreting taxpayer intent.

Ensures proper handling of sensitive taxpayer data and reinforces adherence to disclosure and privacy regulations in all case interactions. Coordinates workflow to ensure efficient case resolution and compliance activities.

Determines staffing needs and develops schedules to ensure adequate coverage and alignment with program requirements, including adherence to workload demands and operational priorities. Advises management on operational issues, risks, and improvement opportunities, and ensures compliance with policies, procedures, and quality standards.
